summary_text: Movilh's XXIV annual report (March 2026) identifies La Araucanía as the region where reported homo/transphobic cases rose most sharply in 2025 — up approximately 150 % year-on-year — during a year when the national total hit a record 3,620 documented cases (+27.1 %). The region's formal trans visibility is extremely low: only 157 people used the Gender Identity Law (21.120) for name and legal-sex rectification in its first three years, indicating a community with minimal institutional presence. Movilh interprets the pattern as the decentralisation of hate toward territories where LGBTIQ+ themes have less public debate, stating this "appears aimed at obstructing" equality work. Against the national 0.72, this is a −0.07 deviation, trend-driven rather than incident-specific. There is no trans-specific Mapuche customary-law jurisdiction or documented state-implicated violence in the dossier; the indigenous-note is structural context within a region under prolonged security conflict. Compared with Tarapacá (0.64), La Araucanía is 0.01 higher: Tarapacá carries a concrete judicial annulment, whereas Araucanía's finding is a statistical acceleration from a low base. Compared with Valparaíso (0.56), it is 0.09 higher despite the 150 % rise, because Araucanía's absolute share (0.72 % of national cases) remains marginal. For a visitor, the practical implication is not a specific hostile incident but the trajectory: the fastest-rising region with the thinnest LGBTI support infrastructure and least public visibility means fewer allies, fewer complaint channels, and a deteriorating climate without institutional counterweight.

sources.title: Informe Anual DDHH: La Araucanía es la región donde más aumentaron los casos y denuncias por homo/transfobia - Araucanía Noticias Temuco
sources.claim_summary: Regional report (24 March 2026) on Movilh's XXIV annual human-rights report: La Araucanía is the region where discrimination complaints based on sexual orientation, gender expression and gender identity rose most in 2025 (about +150 %), within a record national total of 3,620 cases (+27.1 %); the report also flags 2025's breakdown (attacks by strangers, arbitrary police detentions, workplace and educational abuses, institutional exclusions) and a broken cross-party consensus on treating LGBTIQ+ reality as a rights matter.

NOTE: only the report's title pages loaded at fetch time; the underlying document is Movilh's XXIV annual report (facts 2025) — source of the record national figures (3,620 cases, +27.1 %, "23 % of all cases known in the last 24 years"), the regional-rise/decentralisation finding naming La Araucanía, and the national-rollback framing the dossier uses.

sources.title: A 3 años de la entrada en vigencia de la Ley de Identidad de Género 157 personas han realizado cambio de sexo registral en la Araucanía – Araucanía Cuenta
sources.claim_summary: Commemoration of the third anniversary of Law 21.120's entry into force: only 157 people completed registry rectification of name and legal sex in La Araucanía in the law's first three years — a very low formal trans visibility in the same region where complaint counts rose fastest.
